newsitem.title: USA: Salem 2, N.J. nuclear unit moves toward restart.
newsitem.headline: Salem 2, N.J. nuclear unit moves toward restart.

text.p: The 1,106 megawatt (MW) Salem 2 nuclear power unit in Salem, N.J., was exiting its refueling outage as of early Monday, moving to end a shutdown which began in 1995, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.

Salem 2, operated by Public Service Enterprise Group Inc, subsidiary of Newark, N.J.-based Public Service Electric & Gas, was expected to resume power output near July 19, the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
The unit is expected to slowly boost power production through the last half of July and reach full production near the end of the month.
Salem 2 and the adjoining 1,106 MW Salem 1 nuclear unit have been out of service since mid-1995 after the NRC raised concerns over safety at the two units.
The Salem 1 unit is tentatively scheduled to resume service late this year.
